instructions: Does this plan bundle behaviours that could ship as separate tickets, so it should be split before review? Answer yes when the plan holds two or more behaviours that could each be built, verified and shipped on its own and are each worth having without the others, such as separate outcomes an operator would notice, eval rows that fall into independent groups, changes to unrelated modules or verbs, or an "and also" with its own reason; a second change counts when it would pass review as its own ticket, whatever its size or whatever file it shares. Answer no when the plan is one behaviour, even a large one: the change with the tests, docs, diagrams, help text or migration it needs, a refactor or helper it needs, several call sites of one fix or rule, or a check that keeps the new behaviour's output correct and its refusal message are all one behaviour. A follow-up the plan only mentions is not in the plan. When the plan is given as its problems, goals and outcomes, judge its behaviour outcomes: a support or follow-up outcome is never a second behaviour.
